clue.text: As you'd go straight through on the Circle Line?

definitions.text: As you'd go straight through on the Circle Line?

parts.words: As you'd go straight through on the Circle Line?
parts.note: surface reading: travelling on the London Underground's looping Circle Line
setter's reading: a line drawn straight across a circle through its centre

explanation.surface: A Tube passenger wonders how to cut straight across the loop of London's Circle Line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route running in a loop; read geometrically, a line straight through a circle is its diameter, giving the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Going directly across a circle through its centre is travelling along its diameter, hence in that straight-across manner.

clue.text: One line cut but restored as integral

parts.note: Roman numeral one

indicators.note: restoring puts things back together, here rebuilding the letters in a fresh order
a cut shortens something, so the word for line loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single line of text was trimmed but later put back as an essential part.
explanation.walkthrough: LINE is cut to LIN; with I and BUT, those letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inbuilt forms a fixed part of the whole from the outset, just as an integral component does.

clue.text: Measure encountered with indifference, ultimately

parts.note: met is the past tense of meet, to encounter

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word before it is used

parts.note: the last letter of indifference

explanation.surface: A response is weighed up and received with a shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to measure out or allot, and the verb mete itself means to apportion.

clue.text: Source of illumination during Advent or Christmas?

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters running across the end of Advent, or, and the start of Christmas

explanation.surface: Candles or lights shine in the run-up to or on Christmas Day.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp or flaming brand, both ways of giving out light.

clue.text: Duplicitous characters found in Spain since repatriated

indicators.note: characters means letters, and these are found sitting inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters from the end of Spain, all of since and the start of repatriated

explanation.surface: Deceitful people discovered in Spain have since been sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repatriated' tempts as a reversal signal, but the letters read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Insincere describes someone saying what they do not mean, which is the two-faced quality of being deceitful.

clue.text: Seaweed found where shoal gathers, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the phrase supplies the letters

parts.note: the letters across the end of shoal and the start of gathers

explanation.surface: Seaweed grows in the spot where a school of fish congregates.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweeds are marine algae, so a single seaweed plant is one alga.

clue.text: Opportunistically stealing unwrapped gold ingot, maybe?

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible version, so the letters may appear in another order
unwrapping takes off the outer covering, so the first and last letters of the metal are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief seizes a gold bar that has been left lying out of its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwrapped' strips the outside letters from the metal only; the bar itself is kept whole for the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Looting is plundering goods, typically taking advantage of a riot or disaster to steal.

clue.text: They've largely eliminated draughts in the bedroom

definitions.text: They've largely eliminated draughts in the bedroom

parts.note: surface reading: cold air blowing in through gaps around the bedroom window
setter's reading: tablets that have mostly replaced the old sleeping draughts, liquid doses taken at bedtime

explanation.surface: Something has mostly stopped cold air getting into the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: A draught (draft) is also a dose of liquid medicine; bedtime potions have largely given way to tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tablets taken to induce slumber have mostly replaced the old liquid sleeping potions swallowed at bedtime.

clue.text: Unfulfilling meeting with underworld leader

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
meeting a need or demand is satisfying it

explanation.surface: A disappointing encounter with a crime boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld leader' suggests a gangster, but it is the mythological ruler of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dissatisfying leaves one discontented, failing to provide the contentment hoped for.

clue.text: Shellfish best left, or cooked?

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the preceding letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether the best of the shellfish has been left alone or cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobster is a large marine crustacean, a classic example of shellfish served at table.

clue.text: Italians bringing back soldier in fetters

indicators.note: bringing something back returns it the way it came, so the combined letters are read right to left
the soldier is placed inside the fetters, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: irons are shackles or chains
GI is an American private soldier

explanation.surface: Italian troops bring home a captured soldier in chains.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the turnaround applies to the whole result; a GI is an American private.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is the Italian plural for gentlemen or men, so it serves as a word for Italians.

clue.text: Gulf ruler married in Ireland, ultimately disappearing

indicators.note: the marriage abbreviation is set within the shortened country name
the final letter vanishing means the country's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A Gulf sheikh weds in Ireland and then quietly vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: EIRE loses its final E to become EIR, and M goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim prince or commander, the title of rulers of states such as Kuwait and Qatar on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Communication facility, one beside public house

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sign describes a payphone set up next to a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beside' simply places the two pieces next to each other; a public house is a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone is a device or service that lets people talk at a distance, so it is a facility for communicating.

clue.text: King is enfolding sister in embrace

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: to enfold is to wrap around, so the little word goes around the sibling abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written
S is an abbreviation for sister

explanation.surface: A king holds his sister in a fond embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: IS wraps round S to give ISS, which follows K.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss is a touch of the lips given as a sign of affection, and as a noun embrace can mean such a caress.

clue.text: Strength to be found in exotic wines

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, so the word is presented in an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Foreign wines are said to give you vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew is literally a tendon, and figuratively means muscular power or toughness.

clue.text: Robust way to meet public

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
once out, news is public knowledge

explanation.surface: A sturdy approach to meeting ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout describes something strong and sturdy, or a person who is resolute, matching sturdy strength.

clue.text: Somehow certain it will become complex

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, hinting that the following letters are arranged differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is sure that a situation is going to get complicated.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate describes something with many interconnected parts or details, a close synonym of complicated.

clue.text: Agree about question that is featured in complicated case

indicators.note: something featured in a thing appears inside it, so these pieces go within the case
complicated means tangled, so the letters of the case are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
c is short for circa, about
Qu is a common abbreviation for question
ie stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone consents after a query is raised in a difficult legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like the container signal, but it is c for circa; the three short pieces sit together inside the jumbled case.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquiesce is to accept or go along with something without protest, a reluctant way of consenting.

clue.text: Fast getting drunk?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: firmly fixed, as a knot that will not slip
second meaning: informal word for intoxicated

explanation.surface: Someone is quickly becoming inebriated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like speed, but here it means firmly held.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means securely fastened or held firm, and in slang it also describes a person who has had too much alcohol.

clue.text: Germ one found flourishing in squalor

indicators.note: a flourish is an extravagant flowing gesture, so the letters are swung about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A germ thrives in filthy conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: Grime is ingrained dirt, and squalor is a state of filthiness, so the dirt stands for the dirty condition.

clue.text: A region involved in early stage of technological development

indicators.note: involved means intricate or tangled, so the letters are twisted out of order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: One area took part in the first phase of the industrial revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is the prehistoric period when people first smelted iron for tools, following the Bronze Age.

clue.text: Peevish Queen rules out changes — no time

parts.note: Qu. is a dictionary abbreviation for queen

indicators.note: changes signals that the remaining letters swap places into another order
having no time means the abbreviation for time is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cranky queen refuses to allow any changes to her schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rules out' loses its T (time), and the seven letters left are rearranged after QU.
explanation.definitionFit: Querulous means complaining in a whining, petulant way, a close match for irritable or fretful.

clue.text: One needed if force is to be deployed?

definitions.text: One needed if force is to be deployed?

indicators.note: deploying troops spreads them into new positions, so the letters are redistributed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in command is required whenever troops are sent into action.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A commissioned military leader gives the orders without which troops cannot be sent into action.

clue.text: Party held in Israel for pop star

indicators.note: something held in another is enclosed by it, so the party sits inside the country code

parts.note: IL is the international code for Israel
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A celebration is thrown in Israel for a famous singer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a much-adored celebrity, and teen idol or pop idol is a common label for a hit singer.

clue.text: Headdress found over in Ferrara, Italy

indicators.note: turned over, the concealed letters must be read backwards
found in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of Ferrara and start of Italy

explanation.surface: A jewelled headpiece turns up in the Italian city of Ferrara.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled ornamental band worn on the head, so it is a kind of headdress.

clue.text: About to get professional to make copy

parts.note: re means about or concerning
pro is short for professional

explanation.surface: Someone is about to hire an expert to produce a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'About' is a piece of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A repro is a reproduction, a replica of an original item such as furniture or a document.

clue.text: Second Judge to be removed? It's doubtful

indicators.note: the abbreviation for judge is to be taken out of the word for a moment

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment, a second
J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.surface: A second judge is to be dismissed, and someone has their doubts about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal describing the judge, but it is the noun for a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is an informal word for uncertain or questionable, matching doubtful.

clue.text: Touched soft material

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of the verb for perceiving by touch
second meaning: matted fabric made from pressed wool

explanation.surface: Someone ran their hand over a soft fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of feel means handled or sensed with the fingers, and it is also a non-woven cloth of compressed fibres.

clue.text: Initially brisk, light easterly winds were gusting

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so the opening letter of each following word is used

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A weather report on fresh breezes from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Blew is the past tense of blow, describing wind that moved strongly, as gusts were doing.

clue.text: Front-line editorials?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: those who go at the front, heading the line

definitions.note: first definition is adjectival; the answer is a plural noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the main opinion articles of a newspaper

explanation.walkthrough: In British newspapers a leader is the leading article, the paper's editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: People at the head of a line or group are its heads, and a newspaper's opinion pieces are called leading articles.

clue.text: Flier is in place, roughly

indicators.note: roughly suggests something done carelessly or approximately, so the letters are only loosely in order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An aviator or bird is more or less where they should be.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird with a throat pouch, and any bird can be called something that flies.

clue.text: Former striker eager to get them across the line?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the old football name for the main central attacker, now called a striker

definitions.text: eager to get them across the line
definitions.note: a cryptic description of the player rather than a synonym
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the player in the middle of the attack, keen to put the ball over the goal line

explanation.surface: An ex-footballer is keen to get the ball over the goal line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striker' could be a worker on strike, but in football (soccer) it is the main goalscorer; 'them' are the balls the player shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional name for the central attacking position in football is the older term for the modern goalscoring striker.
